scope: Prepared external portable ZIP clean-install and offline authoring helper, compared to actual native first-run verifier and CLI/authoring contracts

findings.title: Extraction follows unchecked installation-parent aliases
findings.evidence: The helper checks only whether the fresh leaf exists, then uses ordinary mkdir/open for PROJECT/installations/... without validating existing parent components or resolved project containment. A preexisting installations junction/symlink redirects extraction and subsequent native execution outside the intended project while the recorded logical installation_ref still appears project-local. ZIP member validation does not protect this existing filesystem ancestry.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate original logical ancestors with the existing link/reparse-safe path guard before directory creation, enforce resolved containment in the intended installations root, and reject any preexisting leaf including broken aliases. Preserve fresh exclusive extraction.
findings.minimal_regression: Controlled owned temporary installation-parent alias or Windows junction to a separate owned target: deny before creating or modifying any target bytes; no native launch.

findings.title: Archive reference and final delivered checksum are not fully bound
findings.evidence: build-result['archive'] is joined and read without first enforcing the fixed expected basename and local build-root containment, allowing absolute or escaping references to be dereferenced. The ZIP is hashed once and then reopened for extraction; final guards verify installed/source package bytes but do not recheck captured build-result bytes or the referenced archive. Replacing the archive after capture, even with a ZIP yielding identical installed bytes, leaves the reported archive checksum disconnected from the final delivered archive.
findings.minimal_fix: Admit the exact canonical archive basename/root before any reference read, validate build identity/revision against the measured subject, capture build-result bytes once, and enforce unchanged captured build-result plus original archive digest immediately before PASS.
minimal_regressions: Absolute/escaping/unexpected archive references reject before a mocked referenced-file read.
Replace build metadata or archive after extraction/smoke using controlled public fixture bytes; final closure rejects even when installed payload bytes are unchanged.

findings.title: Delivered author kit is inventoried without validating emitted commitments
findings.evidence: The helper records JSON from export-capabilities and author-package, then hashes whichever kit files are present. It does not require the actual response statuses, verify exported snapshot bytes against snapshot_hash/current profile, or validate the emitted manifest/payload bytes against the native authoring response. A modified emitted strategy/manifest can therefore be included in version.json while the helper still declares PASS and retains the earlier successful command response.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate exact native response contracts and captured emitted capability/package bytes using the existing snapshot/manifest/payload validators and commitments. Recheck that captured author-kit closure at final PASS instead of merely accepting a newly computed inventory.
findings.minimal_regression: Controlled post-command mutation/deletion of the exported capability file or authored manifest/payload, while leaving the captured native JSON response unchanged, must deny completion.

additional_observations: The helper selects the actual builder's archive basename shape correctly in ordinary successful output, and native verifier report fields product_path/pythonpath/scenario_count match the current contract.

The three source documentation/example paths used for kit creation exist. The engineering example is explicitly identified as not a verified GPT strategy and does not receive research or financial qualification.

The existing first-run verifier performs concrete native hardware, defaults/preservation, owned control/restart, migration, loopback-denial and tamper assertions; its internals were read only as the invoked contract, not independently requalified.
limitations: No helper, test, product/native, build, extraction or network command executed. Only public source/contracts and existence of the three tracked documentation inputs were inspected.
No archive/executable bytes, private DB/auth/config/profile or generated native output directories were read.
This is prepared-tool readiness review with unresolved Important findings, not portable installation evidence or a PASS result.
No PQR, ordinary financial workflow, real cloud/forward, Ubuntu or whole-Master acceptance is issued.
